title: Git History Archaeology: Revision Notes
summary: Quick revision notes on digging through Git history: filtering git log, pickaxe search with -S/-G, git blame and show, and git bisect to find the commit that introduced a bug.

chapters.title: History Archaeology Mental Model
points: Question-to-tool map: 'which commits touched X?' → log filters; 'when did this string appear/vanish?' → log -S/-G; 'who last changed this line?' → blame; 'what did that commit do?' → show; 'which commit broke it?' → bisect
History is a DAG of immutable snapshots; log, blame and show only read it, so they are always safe to run
Default `git log` walks back from HEAD through parents; add a revision range `A..B` (commits in B not in A) to bound the search
Blame shows the last commit to touch a line, not the commit that introduced the idea; follow the chain with `-L` or `blame <sha>^` to go deeper
Always narrow before reading: filter by path, author, date or message first, then inspect single commits with show

chapters.title: Filtering git log
points: `git log --oneline --graph --decorate --all` gives a compact topology view of every branch
Filter by metadata: `--author="name"`, `--since="2 weeks ago"`, `--until=2026-01-01`, `--grep="fix"` (message regex; add -i for case-insensitive)
Path filter after a double dash: `git log -- path/file` limits to commits touching it; add `--follow` to track a single file across renames
`git log -p` adds the patch, `--stat` shows files changed, `--name-status` shows A/M/D/R per file
Commit-shape filters: `--no-merges` hides merge commits, `--merges` shows only them, `-n 5` limits count, `--first-parent` follows only the mainline
Custom output: `--pretty=format:"%h %an %ad %s" --date=short`

chapters.title: Pickaxe Search: log -S, -G and -L
points: `git log -S"foo"` lists commits where the number of occurrences of the string foo changed (added or removed), so it finds when a symbol appeared or vanished
`git log -G"regex"` lists commits whose diff has an added or removed line matching the regex, even when the occurrence count did not change
-S vs -G: -S is a count-change test on a fixed string (add --pickaxe-regex to use a regex); -G matches any changed line, so it is noisier but catches moved or edited lines
Add `-p` to see the matching hunk, and a path after `--` to speed up and narrow the search: `git log -S"MAX_RETRIES" -p -- src/`
`git log -L 10,20:file.c` or `-L :funcName:file.c` shows the full history of a line range or function, with diffs, across renames and moves
Search every branch with `--all`; without it only history reachable from HEAD is searched

chapters.title: git blame and git show
points: `git blame file` prints the last commit, author and date for every line; limit it with `-L 40,60` or `-L :funcName`
Ignore whitespace and moved code: `-w` skips whitespace changes, `-M` detects lines moved within a file, `-C` detects lines copied from other files
Skip bulk-format commits: `git blame --ignore-rev <sha>` or `--ignore-revs-file .git-blame-ignore-revs`, and set `blame.ignoreRevsFile` in config
Blame at an older point: `git blame <sha>^ -- file` re-blames the file as it was just before that commit, to find the previous author of the line
`git show <sha>` prints message plus diff; `git show <sha>:path` prints the file as it was in that commit; `git show --stat <sha>` summarises only
Find the why: take the sha from blame, run `git show <sha>` and read the message, then find the PR or issue it references

chapters.title: git bisect: Binary Search for a Bad Commit
points: Workflow: `git bisect start`, then `git bisect bad` (current commit is broken), then `git bisect good <sha-or-tag>` (known working); Git checks out the midpoint and you mark each one good or bad
Bisect halts after about log2(N) steps (1000 commits ≈ 10 steps) and prints 'first bad commit'; finish with `git bisect reset` to return to your original branch
Shortcut: `git bisect start <bad> <good>`; if the commit can't be tested, use `git bisect skip`
Automate with `git bisect run <cmd>`: exit code 0 = good, 1-127 except 125 = bad, 125 = skip, 128+ aborts; e.g. `git bisect run npm test` or `git bisect run ./check.sh`
Inspect or replay a session: `git bisect log` shows the marks so far, and `git bisect replay <file>` reruns a saved log
Use the terms `git bisect start --term-old=fast --term-new=slow` when hunting something other than a bug, such as a performance change

chapters.title: Archaeology Cheat Sheet
points: Which commits touched a file: `git log --follow -p -- path`
Who last changed a line: `git blame -w -M -L 40,60 file`
When a string was added or removed: `git log -S"str" -p --all`; when a changed line matched a pattern: `git log -G"regex"`
History of a function: `git log -L :funcName:file`
Find the breaking commit: `git bisect start; git bisect bad; git bisect good <sha>; git bisect run ./test.sh; git bisect reset`

Common mistakes: forgetting `git bisect reset`, a test script that returns a wrong exit code, bisecting with a dirty working tree, trusting blame without checking for a reformat commit, and forgetting `--` before a path
